3.problem: ARQ None was treated as accepted even when a retained completed result blocked a new document retry.
implementation: Actual ARQ Job return is accepted. queued/deferred/in_progress duplicates reuse the existing ID.

A document job whose stable ID has a complete retained result submits one fresh :attempt:<uuid> ID and requires actual acceptance. The old result is retained; no blind result deletion or retry loop is introduced.
Unknown/not_found rejection fails explicitly. A rejected fresh attempt also fails explicitly unless a real live duplicate is confirmed. Queue disabled still returns None.
KG/rebuild/reconcile/connector/repair/scan all use the shared strict live-handoff checker. Retained terminal results are explicitly rejected, with no implicit rerun for these workflows.
Removed the scan-only private checker name and used the same actual acceptance owner for all strict entry points.

Updated the three historical KG/rebuild/reconcile duplicate checks to state their live status and expect the confirmed job ID; migrated only this exclusively assigned test file old imports to actual routes-support/chunks/audit owners.
concurrency_contract: processing._get_document/_prepare_retry_document and managed handoff use no SQL row lock or atomic pending compare. Two simultaneous requests that both read a terminal document can create two fresh attempts.

Existing worker document/pipeline Redis coordination still guards execution; once pending is durable, normal and force retries return409. The new finite check confirms force does not override a pending live handoff.
No new active-attempt store, broker state mapping, or new concurrency framework was added.

4.problem: Shared Redis default allkeys-lru could evict ARQ payloads/locks under embedding cache pressure.
implementation: All four actual Redis service commands now default to512mb and maxmemory-policy=noeviction, retaining explicit deployment overrides.

Helm does not install Redis. REDIS_URL value comment and Helm guide state external broker server must use noeviction; no fake application environment variable is introduced to pretend to configure the external server.
Docs explain memory-pressure write errors are visible, capacity/cache release is required, and changing logical Redis databases does not isolate eviction. LRU caches require a separate instance.
Actual ARQ-memory transport test injects OOM ResponseError and confirms it propagates instead of returning an accepted job ID.

5.problem: Unversioned asset0/chunk-index object names let a failed new pipeline overwrite still-active images.
implementation: Four actual production image upload paths now use asset-<full SHA256 of final JPEG bytes> as the opaque chunk_key. Inline and preview reuse their already-computed digest; metadata extraction and ZIP compute it once.

The existing tenant:dataset:document:chunk_key ID and physical directory format remain supported. MinIO uploader, API assets, asset authorization, vision reader, browser citation strings, hierarchy keys, and source document identity are not redefined.

Identical content in the same document can share an immutable object. Different content gets a different ID even when both runs start at index0. Existing numeric/asset0 IDs remain readable and deletable without migration.
Removed the now-unused private extracted-image chunk_index parameter and ZIP idx parameter with their actual call sites; public source metadata/counters remain supported.

At the end of inline/ZIP upload preparation, the existing _record_document_image_ids immediately merges actual uploaded IDs into durable document metadata before later correction/governance/embedding can fail. Empty/no-upload sets do nothing; failed uploads publish no ID.

The recorder unions old active IDs with new actual IDs and refreshes the same worker ORM document, so later metadata projections use the merged aggregate. Existing failure cleanup reloads persisted metadata via populate_existing.

Individual version deletion currently deletes chunks/KG/vector/BM25 only and preserves document image IDs. The actual endpoint finite check deletes one version while shared image bytes remain reachable from the active version. Full document deletion uses the existing aggregate/actual chunk reference cleanup. No new per-version image GC is added.
